abstract: Background: Culex pipiens biotype pipiens (Cx. p. pipiens) is the primary vector of West Nile and Usutu viruses in Europe and overwinters as adult females in shelters, such as cellars. However, the localised environmental and anthropogenic drivers regulating adult behavioural plasticity and the timing of entry into and exit from these overwintering sites remain poorly understood. Methods: Over two consecutive winters (2023-2025) in Northwestern Germany, we monitored the overwintering period of Cx. p. pipiens across an urban-rural gradient using custom interception traps at the entry points (e.g. windows) of overwintering sites (e.g. cellars). We modelled the days of the year at which 10%, 50%, and 90% of cumulative populations entered or exited shelters (Q10, Q50, Q90), against satellite-derived land use and artificial light at night (ALAN), environmental temperature, indoor temperature and relative humidity, cumulative degree-days (CDD), and wing size. Results: In autumn, early entry (Q10) was delayed by 24.1{+/-}7.7 days in semi-urban allotment gardens compared to rural sites. At late entry (Q90), land use effects disappeared, and non-linear deviations from seasonal mean environmental temperatures shaped entry across land uses, while increasing ALAN delayed entry (0.64 days per unit increase). Entry probability increased with cumulative cooling degree-days below 18 {degrees}C. In spring, exit timing was independent of land use but driven by the indoor microclimate. Early exit (Q10) was advanced by higher minimum indoor temperatures (2.35 days per 1 {degrees}C) and higher minimum relative humidity (0.57 days per 1%), with additive land use effects driving earlier emergence in urban than in rural sites. Conversely, higher minimum relative humidity delayed late exit (Q90). Spring exit was best predicted by CDD above 0 {degrees}C. Finally, larger wing centroid size did not affect overwintering survival but delayed spring exit in Cx. p. pipiens. Conclusion: Adult Cx. p. pipiens exhibit behavioural plasticity, shortening their overwintering period in human-altered landscapes. Delayed autumn entry, paired with earlier spring exit driven by urban warming and low thermal thresholds, extends seasonal vector activity. Integrating these complex anthropogenic and microclimatic drivers into surveillance frameworks is vital for predicting early-season pathogen persistence and optimising targeted interventions. Keywords. Cx. pipiens biotype pipiens, phenology, overwintering, land use, artificial light at night, urban heat island
